summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of Crohn’s disease, status post colectomy and ileorectal anastomosis, long-term steroid use, and nephrolithiasis was admitted for increased diarrhea, abdominal pain, and new-onset left flank and testicular pain. Workup revealed a Crohn’s flare confirmed by CT, MRI enterography, and sigmoidoscopy with biopsy, showing inflammation at the anastomosis. A 2-mm non-obstructing kidney stone was noted, possibly contributing to referred pain. Infectious causes were ruled out. Acute kidney injury (creatinine 1.3 mg/dL) was attributed to dehydration and resolved with IV fluids. Pain was managed with IV hydromorphone, later transitioned to oral. The patient improved clinically, with diarrhea resolving to baseline and pain controlled. He was discharged home on prednisone 40 mg daily pending GI follow-up, a 10-day course of ciprofloxacin, cyclobenzaprine, lidocaine patch, and hydromorphone for breakthrough pain, with instructions to discontinue tizanidine and follow up on an incidental finding of an enlarged left groin vessel.
problems: Unspecified hereditary and idiopathic peripheral neuropathy
